say: Look at these. Bird, butterfly, elephant. Which one can NOT fly?
why: An elephant is too heavy to fly; birds and butterflies have wings.

say: Cow, fish, hen. Which one lives in the water?
why: A fish has fins and gills, so it lives in water.

prompt: Which one is not a fruit?
say: Mango, banana, carrot. Two are fruits. Which one is NOT a fruit?
why: A carrot is a vegetable; it grows under the ground.

say: Bus, boat, horse. Which one rolls on wheels?
why: A bus has wheels; a boat floats and a horse has legs.

prompt: Which one doesn't belong in a kitchen?
say: Pan, spoon, bed. Which one does NOT belong in the kitchen?
why: A bed belongs in the bedroom; we cook with pans and spoons.

prompt: Which one is not an animal?
say: Monkey, tree, squirrel. Which one is NOT an animal?
why: A tree is a plant; monkeys and squirrels are animals.

prompt: Which one goes on our feet?
say: Socks, cap, gloves. Which one do we wear on our feet?
why: Socks go on feet; a cap goes on the head and gloves on hands.

say: Duck, fish, cat. Which one does not like to swim at all?
why: Most cats stay away from water; ducks and fish are great swimmers.

prompt: Which one is not a vehicle?
say: Car, bicycle, tree. Which one can NOT take you somewhere?
why: A tree stays in one place; cars and bicycles carry us.

prompt: These go together. Which one too?
say: Apple, strawberry, cherry. What is the same about them? Which one belongs with them?
why: They are all red, and the rose is red too!

say: Car, bus, bicycle. They all go on the road. Which one also goes on the road?
why: A truck drives on the road; a boat sails and a plane flies.

prompt: Which one joins the sea friends?
say: Fish, octopus, dolphin. They all live in the sea. Who else lives there?
why: A crab lives in the sea too.

prompt: Which one belongs in the sky?
say: Sun, star, moon. Where do we see them? Which one also belongs up there?
why: Clouds are up in the sky with the sun, moon and stars.

say: Banana, corn, lemon. What colour are they all? Pick one more of that colour.
why: A sunflower is yellow, just like the banana, corn and lemon.

prompt: Which one is also for sport?
say: Football, cricket bat, basketball. We play games with them. Which one too?
why: A tennis ball is for playing a sport too.

say: Cow, goat, sheep. They all live on a farm. Which one also lives on a farm?
why: A pig lives on a farm too; a dolphin lives in the sea.

prompt: What is the opposite of big?
say: An elephant is big. Which animal is SMALL?
why: An ant is tiny, the opposite of a big elephant.

prompt: What is the opposite of day?
say: The sun shines in the day. What do we see at NIGHT?
why: Night is the opposite of day; the moon comes out at night.

prompt: What is the opposite of happy?
say: This face is happy. Which face is the opposite?
why: Sad is the opposite of happy.

prompt: What is the opposite of hot?
say: Fire is very hot. Which one is very COLD?
why: Snow is cold, the opposite of hot fire.

prompt: What is the opposite of up?
say: This arrow points up. Which arrow points the opposite way?
why: Down is the opposite of up.

prompt: What is the opposite of open?
say: This lock is open. Which one is the opposite?
why: A closed lock is the opposite of an open lock.

prompt: What is the opposite of fast?
say: An aeroplane is very fast. Which one is SLOW?
why: A tortoise walks slowly, the opposite of fast.

prompt: What comes out of the egg?
say: A hen sat on this egg. Crack! What comes out?
why: A baby chick hatches from a hen's egg.

prompt: What happens to ice cream in sun?
say: The ice cream sits in the hot sun for a long time. What happens to it?
why: The sun's heat melts ice cream into a drippy puddle.

prompt: We forgot to water it. What happens?
say: We forgot to water this flower for many days. What will it look like?
why: Plants droop and dry up without water.

prompt: Dark clouds! What should we carry?
say: Big dark clouds are in the sky. What should we take outside?
why: Dark clouds often bring rain, so an umbrella keeps us dry.

say: This little caterpillar eats and eats, then sleeps in a cocoon. What does it become?
why: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

say: You let go of a ball up high. Which way does it go?
why: Things fall down to the ground; that pull is called gravity.

say: Someone opened an umbrella. Why do you think they did that?
why: We open an umbrella when it rains.

prompt: What will the mango seed grow into?
say: We plant a mango seed in the soil and water it for a long, long time. What grows?
why: A mango seed grows into a big mango tree.

say: Oops! A glass falls on a hard floor. What might happen?
why: Glass can break when it falls, so we hold it with two hands.

prompt: The dog is hungry. What does it want?
say: What if the dog is very hungry? What would it want?
why: A hungry dog wants food, like a bone.

prompt: The car has no petrol. Now what?
say: What if the car has no petrol? Where should it go?
why: A car needs petrol from the petrol pump to move.

prompt: It's very cold. What do we wear?
say: What if it is very, very cold outside? What should we wear?
why: A warm jacket keeps our body warm.

prompt: It's night time. What do we do?
say: The moon is out and it is late at night. What should we do?
why: Night is for sleeping so our body can rest and grow.

prompt: What if there was no water?
say: What if there was no water at all? Who would be in trouble?
why: Plants, animals and people all need water to live.

say: Look carefully. Which one has the MOST sweets?
why: Three sweets is more than one or two.

say: Elephant, mouse, bird. Which one is the heaviest?
why: An elephant is the heaviest land animal of all.

say: Giraffe, dog, cat. Which animal is the tallest?
why: A giraffe's long neck makes it very tall.

prompt: Which one holds the most water?
say: Bathtub, glass, spoon. Which one holds the MOST water?
why: A bathtub is much bigger, so it holds the most water.

say: Aeroplane, bicycle, tortoise. Which one is the fastest?
why: An aeroplane zooms through the sky faster than all of them.

say: Watermelon, grapes, cherry. Which fruit is the biggest?
why: A watermelon is much bigger than grapes or cherries.

say: Snake, caterpillar, ant. Which one is the longest?
why: A snake is much longer than a caterpillar or an ant.

prompt: Which shape fits the round hole?
say: Here is a round hole. Which shape would fit inside it?
why: A circle fits a round hole; corners would get stuck.

say: Which arrow points UP to the sky?
why: This arrow points up, towards the sky.

say: Put one triangle on top of the other, flat sides touching. What shape do they make?
why: Two triangles joined at their flat sides make a diamond.

say: Apple, banana, apple, banana, apple. What comes next?
why: The pattern goes apple, banana, so banana comes next.

say: Sun, moon, sun, moon, sun. What comes next?
why: Day and night take turns, so the moon comes next.

say: Star, star, moon. Star, star. What comes next?
why: The pattern is star, star, moon, so the moon comes next.

say: Dog, cat, cat. Dog, cat. What comes next?
why: The pattern is dog, cat, cat, so another cat comes next.

say: Red, blue, blue. Red, blue. Listen to the pattern. What comes next?
why: The pattern is red, blue, blue, so blue comes next.

say: I have a long trunk, but I am not a tree. Who am I?
why: An elephant's nose is called a trunk.

say: I say moo, and I give you milk. Who am I?
why: A cow says moo and gives us milk.

prompt: Riddle: I shine in the sky
say: I am yellow, I am hot, and I shine up in the sky. What am I?
why: The sun is hot and shines in the sky.

prompt: Riddle: I have hands, no fingers
say: I have two hands but no fingers, and I tell you the time. What am I?
why: A clock has hands that point to the time.

prompt: Riddle: up when rain comes down
say: I go UP when the rain comes DOWN. What am I?
why: We put an umbrella up when the rain comes down.

say: Let's count the mangoes together. How many?
why: One, two, three. Three mangoes!

say: Count the stars. Touch each one with your eyes.
why: One, two, three, four, five. Five stars!

say: It's Diwali! Count the lamps. How many?
why: One, two, three, four. Four lamps!

say: Which one has the FEWEST cookies?
why: One cookie is fewer than two or three.

say: Two bananas, and one more banana. How many now?
why: Two and one more makes three.

prompt: One bird flies away. How many?
say: Three birds sit on a branch. One flies away. How many are left?
why: Three take away one leaves two.

say: In cricket you hit a four! Then one more run. How many runs?
why: Four and one more makes five runs.

say: Let's count by tens: ten, twenty, thirty... What comes next?
why: Counting by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40!

say: Ten, twenty, something, forty. Which number is missing?
why: 10, 20, 30, 40. Thirty was missing.

say: Eighteen, nineteen... what comes next?
why: After nineteen comes twenty.

say: Seven, three, five. Which number is the biggest?
why: Seven is more than five and three.

say: What number is one LESS than ten?
why: Count back from ten: nine is one less.

prompt: How many legs does a dog have?
say: How many legs does a dog walk on?
why: A dog has four legs.

prompt: How many wheels on a bicycle?
say: An auto-rickshaw has three wheels. How many wheels does a bicycle have?
why: A bicycle has two wheels; 'bi' means two.

say: Which hand shows FIVE fingers?
why: An open hand shows five fingers.

say: Three fish. Which group has the SAME number?
why: Three apples and three fish: the same number!

prompt: How many on the empty plate?
say: Look at this empty plate. How many sweets are on it?
why: Nothing on the plate means zero.

prompt: Share four sweets with two friends
say: Four sweets, shared fairly between two friends. How many does each friend get?
why: Two for you and two for me: that's fair sharing.

say: Ball starts with /b/. Bee, fish, apple. Which one starts like ball?
why: Bee and ball both start with /b/.

say: Mango starts with /m/. Monkey, dog, cat. Which starts like mango?
why: Monkey and mango both start with /m/.

say: Sun starts with /s/. Snake, cow, moon. Which starts like sun?
why: Snake and sun both start with /s/.

say: Cat starts with /k/. Car, dog, fish. Which starts like cat?
why: Car and cat both start with /k/.

say: Dog starts with /d/. Duck, cat, banana. Which starts like dog?
why: Duck and dog both start with /d/.

say: Fish starts with /f/. Frog, bee, egg. Which starts like fish?
why: Frog and fish both start with /f/.

say: Pen starts with /p/. Pig, cow, apple. Which starts like pen?
why: Pig and pen both start with /p/.

say: A says /a/. Apple, banana, mango. Which starts with A?
why: Apple starts with A, /a/ /a/ apple.

say: T says /t/. Tiger, dog, elephant. Which starts with T?
why: Tiger starts with T, /t/ /t/ tiger.

say: Egg. /e/ /e/ egg. Which letter does egg start with?
why: Egg starts with the letter e.

say: Cat... hat, dog, sun. Which one rhymes with cat?
why: Cat and hat rhyme: they both end in -at.

say: Bee... tree, fish, car. Which one rhymes with bee?
why: Bee and tree rhyme: they both end in -ee.

say: Star... car, moon, fish. Which one rhymes with star?
why: Star and car rhyme: they both end in -ar.

say: Mouse... house, cow, banana. Which one rhymes with mouse?
why: Mouse and house rhyme: they both end in -ouse.

say: Dog ends with /g/. Frog, cat, sun. Which one ends like dog?
why: Frog and dog both end with /g/.

prompt: What does a seed need to grow?
say: A tiny seed wants to grow big. What does it need?
why: Seeds need water, sunlight and soil to grow.

say: We drop these in a bucket of water. Leaf, hammer, key. Which one floats?
why: A leaf is light, so it floats; metal things sink.

say: Pitter patter! Where does rain fall from?
why: Rain falls from clouds full of tiny water drops.

say: Bees buzz from flower to flower. What yummy thing do they make?
why: Bees make honey from flower nectar.

say: Hen, cow, dog. Which one lays eggs?
why: Hens lay eggs; cows and dogs have babies that drink milk.

prompt: What will melt in the sun?
say: Snowman, tree, car. Which one melts in the hot sun?
why: Snow is frozen water; heat turns it back to water.

say: A little chick says cheep cheep. Who is its mother?
why: A chick is a baby hen.

prompt: What helps you smell a flower?
say: Sniff sniff! What helps you smell this flower?
why: We smell with our nose.

say: La la la! What helps you hear music?
why: We hear with our ears.

prompt: What grows on a coconut tree?
say: Look at this tall palm tree near the beach. What grows on it?
why: Coconuts grow high up on coconut palm trees.

prompt: Which one will a magnet pull?
say: A magnet pulls some metal things. Paper clip, banana, teddy. Which one?
why: A magnet pulls things made of iron, like a paper clip.

say: India's national bird has beautiful long feathers. Which one is it?
why: The peacock is India's national bird.

say: Tree, car, house. Which one is alive and grows?
why: A tree is alive: it drinks water, grows and makes seeds.

say: Big tree, tiny sprout, small plant. Which one came FIRST?
why: Every tree starts as a tiny sprout from a seed.

say: Banana, lollipop, fizzy drink. Which one is healthy for breakfast?
why: Fruit gives our body energy and vitamins.

prompt: What do we use before eating?
say: Before we eat, we wash our hands. What do we use?
why: Soap and water wash away germs before we eat.

prompt: Which one is bad for teeth?
say: Lollipop, carrot, milk. Which one can hurt our teeth if we eat too much?
why: Sticky sweets stay on teeth, so we brush after eating them.

say: At the traffic light, which colour says STOP?
why: Red means stop; green means go.

prompt: What do we wear on a bike?
say: When we ride a bicycle, what do we wear on our head?
why: A helmet keeps our head safe if we fall.

prompt: Which one is not safe to touch?
say: Fire, teddy, book. Which one is NOT safe to touch?
why: Fire is very hot and can burn; we stay away.

prompt: Which one is safe to play with?
say: Ball, knife, plug socket. Which one is safe to play with?
why: A ball is safe; knives and plugs are only for grown-ups.

prompt: Lost in a shop. Who do you ask?
say: If you cannot find Amma or Appa in a shop, who can you ask for help?
why: Stay where you are and ask a police officer, a shop worker or a mother with children.

say: You are thirsty after playing. Which drink is best?
why: Water is the best drink for a thirsty body.

say: Before we cross the road with a grown-up, what do we do?
why: We stop and look both ways for cars.

prompt: Which food helps you grow strong?
say: Broccoli, doughnut, chips. Which one helps you grow strong?
why: Vegetables help our body grow strong.

say: Someone you do not know offers you sweets. What should you do?
why: Say no, and go tell Amma, Appa or your teacher.

say: It's bedtime. What helps you sleep well?
why: A cosy bed, without screens or sweets, helps us sleep.

say: Which face is HAPPY?
why: A happy face has a big smile.

say: Yawn! Which face is SLEEPY?
why: A sleepy face has closed eyes, ready for bed.

say: Wow! Which face looks SURPRISED?
why: A surprised face has big eyes and an open mouth.

say: The little puppy is out in the rain, all wet and alone. How does the puppy feel?
why: A cold, wet puppy feels sad; we can give it a dry towel.

prompt: Your friend fell. How do they feel?
say: Your friend fell down and hurt their knee. How do they feel?
why: Falling hurts, so your friend may feel sad. We can help them up.

prompt: It's a birthday! How do they feel?
say: It's your friend's birthday party! How does your friend feel?
why: Birthdays make us feel happy and excited.

prompt: Your friend is sad. What helps?
say: Your friend is crying. What can you do to help?
why: A kind hug or kind words help a sad friend feel better.

say: When you feel angry, what can help your body calm down?
why: Slow, deep breaths help our body calm down.

prompt: Ajji gives you a mango. You say…?
say: Ajji gives you a sweet mango. What do you say?
why: We say thank you when someone is kind to us.

say: Ajji's shopping bag is very heavy. What can you do?
why: Helping someone carry a heavy bag is kind.

prompt: You shared your toy. Friend feels…?
say: You shared your toy with your friend. How does your friend feel?
why: Sharing makes our friends feel happy.

prompt: The kitten is hungry. It wants…?
say: The kitten is meowing. It is hungry. What does it want?
why: A hungry kitten wants food or milk; animals have feelings too.

prompt: Someone took your toy. You feel…?
say: Someone took your toy without asking. How might you feel? There is no wrong answer.
why: It's okay to feel sad or cross; we use words to say how we feel.

say: If you could fly like a bird, where would you go? Pick any one!
why: What a wonderful trip! Tell Amma or Appa what you'd see there.

say: If you could have any pet, which one would you pick?
why: Great choice! Every pet needs love, food and water.

say: If you had lots of blocks, what would you build?
why: Super builder! Maybe you can build it for real later.

say: If you could be an animal for one day, which one?
why: Can you move like that animal? Show Amma!

prompt: Pick a colour for the rangoli
say: We're making a Diwali rangoli! Which colour should we use first?
why: Beautiful! Every colour makes a rangoli bright.

prompt: What would you pack for the moon?
say: You are going on a rocket to the moon! What would you take?
why: Good packing! Astronauts take the things they need most.

prompt: Who is the hero of your story?
say: Let's make up a story! Who should be the hero?
why: A great hero! What brave or kind thing do they do?

prompt: What would a cloud taste like?
say: If you could taste a fluffy cloud, what would it taste like?
why: Yum! Real clouds are made of tiny water drops.

prompt: Where would a tiny ant live?
say: If you were a tiny ant, where would you make your home?
why: What a cosy home! Real ants live in tunnels under the ground.

prompt: Mix two fruits! How does it taste?
say: Imagine a fruit that is half mango and half banana! How would it taste?
why: Mango-nana! You just invented a new fruit.
